sources.name: Diligent Robotics — Moxi product and mobile manipulation
Diligent Robotics — MoxiFAQ;RaaS,locking and charging dock
Diligent Robotics — October1,2019marketlaunch press release republished by issuer

highlights: Hospital logistics for non-patient-facing tasks such as supply and lab-sample delivery
Mobile manipulation combines an arm and hand with navigation through hospital spaces
Implementation team configures workflows; human-guided learning supports adaptation

The FAQ describes locking compartments and automatic travel to a charging dock. Robot-as-a-service pricing is tailored to the hospital; no exact purchase/subscription price, full-charge duration or original-generation endurance is established.

Providence’s February 2024 implementation account describes three locked drawers and controller-guided mapping by Diligent staff over about three days. Its March 2024 report confirms two robots in use. Mapping/setup is distinct from later autonomous operation and these are original deployment findings, not Moxi 2.0 specifications.

The manufacturer’s September 2026 UTMB case study reports about 70000 deliveries and 22000 delivery hours with three robots, about 25 deliveries per robot per day. These are cumulative/site figures, not battery endurance, universal throughput or proof of a 2.0 hardware upgrade.

The September 2026 Shannon Health case study reports more than 100000 deliveries, about 30000 delivery hours and two robots, averaging about 27 deliveries per robot per day. Vendor-published staff accounts and savings estimates are not independent clinical outcomes or guaranteed workforce replacement.

The 2022 issuer history dates Moxi’s debut to 2018 and first commercial deployments to 2020; the issuer’s October 1, 2019 press release announces a market rollout beginning October 2. These are different historical milestones whose commercial-timeline wording is not silently reconciled into one shipping date.

Clinical staff load/unload and remain responsible for care. Locked transport bins and obstacle-aware navigation do not prove diagnosis, treatment, infection prevention or zero-collision operation. Existing 136 kg mass and generic large-size label lack support in the selected sources and are omitted.

highlights: The August 17, 2026 rollout identifies NVIDIA-powered A2000 compute and claims 10 times onboard compute with 10–15 times faster perception versus the previous generation. These are supplier-relative compute/perception claims, not travel speed, delivery throughput or independent benchmark results.

Manufacturer distinguishes up to nine hours at a time from up to 18 operating hours per day. Recharging between runs is not an 18-hour single-charge guarantee; the 30 percent faster charging claim supplies neither an absolute full-charge duration nor a defined test baseline.

All safety and autonomy behaviors run onboard according to the launch release, with cellular fallback available for Wi-Fi dead zones. AWS cloud infrastructure trains the World Model; private 5G hospital deployments are a plan, not proof of already installed private 5G or total network/cloud independence.

Expanded cameras, sensors and redesigned storage drawers, handles and service ergonomics are named upgrades. The release does not establish exact robot mass, body dimensions, arm payload, gripper model or numerical joint count; original-generation figures are not inherited.

The rollout names Endeavor Health Edward Hospital, Providence Saint John’s Health Center and Children’s Hospital Los Angeles. The manufacturer says it is accepting orders; hospital stories and cumulative fleet deliveries do not establish universal outcomes or complete geographic availability.

October 28, 2025 plans described NVIDIA Thor/IGX Thor and future robot foundation models; August 2026 rollout specifies A2000 and a World Model. The newer source governs the described rollout, while future modular compute upgrades and 15-plus-robots-per-hospital aspirations remain plans.

companyFocus.name: Diligent Robotics
companyFocus.role: Hospital-logistics mobile manipulation robots;historical non-commercial research precursor
highlights: Founded in 2017 by Andrea Thomaz and Vivian Chu according to the company. Original Moxi, Moxi 2.0 and historical non-commercial Poli retain separate scopes; Poli’s University of Texas research lineage is explicit rather than presenting every platform as a current commercial product.

Diligent is identified as a Serve Robotics company in the August 2026 rollout and republished parent-company blog. Ownership does not merge the Diligent and Serve brands or transfer sidewalk-robot specifications. The exact legal closing date is not inferred from inconsistent announcement/blog timing or blocked investor filings. Embodied Moxie remains a separate company/product.

Manufacturer FAQ describes robot-as-a-service, locking compartments, automatic charging-dock travel and site-specific hospital workflows. Staff perform clinical care and load/unload materials; no exact service price, universal patient-outcome benefit or infection-prevention certification is established.

The 2025 Moxi 2.0 Thor plan and actual 2026 A2000 rollout are different milestones. Up to 9 hours at a time is distinct from 18 operating hours per day, and 30 percent faster charging is not a full-charge duration. Private 5G and larger future fleets remain plans; World Model/cloud training software is not an additional hardware model.

September 2026 UTMB/Shannon case studies are manufacturer-published cumulative/site metrics, not independent tests or proof that each deployed robot is Moxi 2.0. Providence’s 2024 articles are deployment-owner accounts with human-guided initial mapping; these source roles remain distinct. University paper links Poli research to the company without transferring other team robots/components to Diligent.
